Я доработал промпт в файле prompts/prompt_eda.txt
Доработай файл eda.ipynb в папке outputs/eda согласно новому промпту

We need read the updated prompt file to see changes, compare with current notebook, then modify notebook accordingly. Must not use /tmp, only project. Need inspect prompt diff. Let's read prompts/prompt_eda.txt.

state.output:
<path>/home/neferpitu/recsys/exam/Quize/prompts/prompt_eda.txt</path>
<type>file</type>
<content>
1: Ты - senior data analyst. Твоя задача - выполнить только EDA (exploratory data analysis) по датасету рекомендательной системы sweet.tv, который лежит в папке data_par/raw/ в формате parquet, и сохранить все артефакты в outputs/eda/. Никакого моделирования (кроме референсных бейзлайнов), обучения сложных моделей, подбора гиперпараметров и генерации submission на этом этапе делать не нужно.
2: 
3: 1. Входные данные:
4: - Папка data_par/raw/. Сначала выполни ls -la / Path.glob("*.parquet") и зафиксируй список файлов, их размеры и число строк.
5: - Ожидаемые сущности:
6:   - dataset11-30week.parquet с колонками user_id, vsetv_id (это channel_id из schedule), start_time, stop_time, duraton (опечатка в названии, читать как duration).
7:   - Три файла schedule с колонками channel_id, channel_title, start_time, duration, tv_show_title, tv_show_id, tv_show_category, tv_show_genre_1..3, year_of_production, director, actors. Один файл - тренировочные недели 11-20, второй - 21-30, третий - тестовые 31-42.
8:   - Возможно, рядом лежит submission.csv. Если найдешь, загрузи только для подсчета пользователей (не записывай submission).
9: - Если фактическая схема отличается от ожидаемой, не выдумывай, выведи в stdout реальные df.columns и dtypes и работай по факту. Обработай оба варианта названий (stop_time/end_time, duraton/duration), если они встречаются.
10: - Важные факты:
11:   - vsetv_id в view log - то же самое, что channel_id в schedule; join идет по (channel, пересечение интервалов).
12:   - tv_show_id = 0 - "нерелевантное ТВ", его надо исключать при построении item-каталога и анализе метаданных.
13:   - Тест (недели 31-42) содержит строго 5 программ на пользователя, отсортированных DESC по частоте (#1 - самая частая). Это важно для будущей метрики MAP@5.
14:   - **Test weeks (31-42) are strictly in the future relative to training weeks (11-30).** Согласно правилам экзамена: "Never use future viewing behaviour... The test-period schedule may be used only to know which programme airs on which channel at which time". Не используй тестовые недели для любых расчетов, кроме справочника программ.
15:   - Ожидаемая разметка ground-truth (из описания соревнования на Kaggle) строилась по правилу: screen_time_ratio = watched_time / show_duration, порог >= 0.8. **Важно:** В правилах экзамена этого порога нет, экзамен требует построить нормировку самому. Поэтому 0.8 здесь — это лишь один из кандидатов (candidate threshold), а не жесткое правило. В EDA не восстанавливай эти 5 программ, но включи это правило в раздел D.
16: 
17: 2. Куда сохранять:
18: - Итоговый файл - один файл outputs/eda/eda.ipynb, который открывается и запускается в Jupyter Notebook без правок.
19: - Дополнительно разрешена папка outputs/eda/figures с PNG-графиками.
20: - Никаких report.md, отдельных *.csv, run.log, environment.txt и прочих файлов в папке outputs/eda/ быть не должно. Все таблицы печатаются в ноутбуке через display(df), все версии пакетов и системная информация выводятся в первой ячейке ноутбука.
21: - Ноутбук должен быть самодостаточным и идемпотентным: при выполнении Run All он пересоздает графики в outputs/eda/figures/ и все ячейки выполняются без ошибок.
22: 
23: 3. Требования к структуре ipynb:
24: - Создай ноутбук через nbformat (или вручную как валидный .ipynb JSON). Обязательно исполни его перед сдачей: jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute --inplace outputs/eda/eda.ipynb. Убедись, что после исполнения cell.outputs у кодовых ячеек непустые там, где ожидаются.
25: - Ноутбук начинается с markdown заголовка "# EDA - sweet.tv TV program recommender", затем идут ячейки в таком порядке:
26: 1. Markdown ## Environment. Первая кодовая ячейка: все импорты, которые понадобятся в этом ноутбуке целиком. Плюс вывод версий python и ключевых пакетов, ОС, числа CPU, объема RAM.
27: 2. Markdown ## Configuration. Вторая кодовая ячейка: глобальные константы и конфигурации.
28:   - Путь к папке с данными (RAW_DIR)
29:   - Путь к папке, в которую будут сохранятся графики (FIG_DIR)
30:   - Seed = 42 - только для ячеек, которые явно сэмплируют данные.
31:   - Стиль графиков
32:   - Разумные лимиты для отображения таблиц
33:   - Список ожидаемых колонок и предполагаемые пути файлов.
34:   - Словарь кандидатных порогов overlap.
35: 3. Markdown ## Data loading and type conversion. Кодовые ячейки: загрузка всех parquet, явное приведение типов.
36:   - **КРИТИЧЕСКИ ВАЖНО (Mojibake):** Проверь текстовые колонки на наличие Mojibake (кракозябр). Выведи `repr(df['tv_show_title'].iloc[0])`. Если увидишь строки вида `Р"РµС...` или `??????`, примени функцию обратного перекодирования `def fix_mojibake(text): return text.encode('cp1251').decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')` к текстовым колонкам (channel_title, tv_show_title, tv_show_category, tv_show_genre_*, director, actors). Если это не помогает, выведи предупреждение и оставь как есть.
37:   - user_id, vsetv_id, channel_id, tv_show_id - int64
38:   - start_time, stop_time/end_time, duration в schedule - datetime64[ns] для времен, int64 для секунд
39:   - tv_show_category, tv_show_genre_1..3, channel_title - category
40:   - duraton/duration в view log - int64
41:   - После приведения выведи df.dtypes и .head(5) для каждого файла.
42:   - Здесь же markdown ячейка ## Conclusion. В ней должно быть только слово "Conclusion".
43: 4. Далее - разделы A-H из пункта 5, каждый как последовательность:
44:   - markdown-заголовок раздела
45:   - кодовые ячейки (не сваливай весь раздел в одну мега-ячейку)
46:   - markdown-ячейка ## Conclusion.
47: 5. Финальный раздел ## Notes and caveats - markdown ячейка без Conclusion, куда нужно записать только фактически наблюдаемые ограничения (например: покрытие view log по неделям, отсутствие negative feedback в логе, необходимость нормализации по duration). Никаких выводов и рекомендаций, только факты.
48: 
49: - Каждый смысловой шаг - отдельная кодовая ячейка.
50: - Никаких %matplotlib inline магии. Используй plt.show() после каждого графика и plt.savefig(FIG_DIR / name, bbox_inches="tight") перед plt.show().
51: - Каждый plt.savefig - с уникальным именем файла и префиксом номера раздела латиницей, snake_case.
52: 
53: 4. Требования к языку и отображению:
54: - Весь текст в markdown, комментариях, print, заголовках графиков, подписях осей, легендах - СТРОГО на английском языке.
55: - В самом коде и тексте ноутбука не должно быть кириллицы. Если в данных (названия передач, категории) есть кириллица, для вывода в графиках используй ASCII-безопасное отображение: `text.encode('ascii', 'replace').decode('ascii')` (заменяй на '?'). Это нужно, чтобы matplotlib не падал с ошибками шрифтов.
56: 
57: 5. Обязательные разделы EDA:
58: A. File overview
59: - Таблица по каждому parquet: имя файла, размер на диске, n_rows, n_cols, memory_usage(deep=True), df.dtypes, число NaN по колонкам, min/max по временным колонкам, df.head(5)
60: - Pie/bar chart: доля строк view log vs три schedule-файла
61: - PNG: 01_file_overview.png
62: 
63: B. View log profile
64: - Уникальные user_id и vsetv_id; их распределение по неделям (start_time.dt.isocalendar().week)
65: - describe() + перцентили (50, 90, 95, 99, 99.9) для duration; количество записей с duraton <= 0 и с duraton > 4*3600 - аномалии
66: - Гистограмма duraton в обычной и log-x шкалах; отдельный boxplot по неделям
67: - Распределение числа просмотров на пользователя и на канал (hist, log-x, log-y), два отдельных графика
68: - Распределение по часам суток (bar) и по дням недели (bar)
69: - Временной диапазон start_time (min/max), bar по неделям
70: - PNG: 5 картинок (02_..., 03_... и т.д.)
71: 
72: C. Schedule profile (по каждому из трех файлов)
73: - **Дедупликация:** Объедини 3 файла расписания в один DataFrame. Проверь и удали дубликаты на стыках файлов по ключу `["channel_id", "start_time"]`. Выведи число удаленных дубликатов.
74: - Число строк, уникальные channel_id, уникальные tv_show_id при tv_show_id != 0.
75: - **Фильтрация:** Для всех графиков категорий и жанров используй ТОЛЬКО размеченные строки (`tv_show_id != 0`). Не смешивай с неразмеченным эфиром.
76: - Доля строк с tv_show_id != 0 - выведи точное значение для каждого файла.
77: - Распределение duration программы
78: - Топ-10 tv_show_category и Топ-20 tv_show_genre_1 (bar, отдельные графики)
79: - Временной диапазон start_time, разбивка строк по неделям

+"""Reusable data helpers for the sweet.tv recommender project."""
+
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+
+RATIO_THRESHOLD = 0.8
+
+try:
+    import pytest
+except ImportError:
+    pytest = None
+
+def _mark_skip_without_pytest(func):
+    """Mark a pytest-style test as skipped when pytest is unavailable."""
+    func.__test__ = False
+    func.__unittest_skip__ = True
+    func.__unittest_skip_why__ = "pytest is not installed"

+
+_requires_pytest = (
+    _mark_skip_without_pytest if pytest is None else (lambda func: func)
+)
+

+def to_epoch_seconds(series):
+    """Convert a datetime-like Series to integer Unix seconds."""
+    return series.astype("datetime64[ns]").astype("int64") // 10**9
+
+
+def merge_overlapping_views(views_df):
+    """Merge overlapping view intervals for each (user_id, vsetv_id) pair.
+
+    Intervals are sorted by start time and merged when the next start is
+    strictly earlier than the running maximum stop. Intervals that only touch
+    at an endpoint are kept separate. The returned duration is the merged
+    interval length in seconds.
+    """
+    columns = ["user_id", "vsetv_id", "start_time", "stop_time", "duration"]
+    missing = [column for column in columns if column not in views_df.columns]
+    if missing:
+        raise ValueError(f"Missing required view columns: {missing}")
+
+    if views_df.shape[0] == 0:
+        empty = views_df.loc[:, columns].copy()
+        empty["user_id"] = empty["user_id"].astype("uint64")
+        empty["vsetv_id"] = empty["vsetv_id"].astype("int64")
+        empty["start_time"] = empty["start_time"].astype("datetime64[ns]")
+        empty["stop_time"] = empty["stop_time"].astype("datetime64[ns]")
+        empty["duration"] = empty["duration"].astype("int64")
+        return empty.reset_index(drop=True)
+
+    frame = views_df.loc[:, ["user_id", "vsetv_id", "start_time", "stop_time"]].copy()
+    frame["start_s"] = to_epoch_seconds(frame["start_time"])
+    frame["stop_s"] = to_epoch_seconds(frame["stop_time"])
+    frame = frame.sort_values(
+        ["user_id", "vsetv_id", "start_s", "stop_s"], kind="mergesort"
+    ).reset_index(drop=True)
+
+    keys = ["user_id", "vsetv_id"]
+    previous_max_stop = frame.groupby(keys, sort=False)["stop_s"].cummax().shift(1)
+    group_change = (
+        frame["user_id"].ne(frame["user_id"].shift())
+        | frame["vsetv_id"].ne(frame["vsetv_id"].shift())
+    )
+    new_segment = group_change | frame["start_s"].ge(previous_max_stop)
+    frame["segment_id"] = new_segment.cumsum()
+
+    merged = frame.groupby("segment_id", sort=False).agg(
+        user_id=("user_id", "first"),
+        vsetv_id=("vsetv_id", "first"),
+        start_s=("start_s", "min"),
+        stop_s=("stop_s", "max"),
+    ).reset_index(drop=True)
+
+    merged["start_time"] = pd.to_datetime(merged["start_s"], unit="s").astype(
+        "datetime64[ns]"
+    )
+    merged["stop_time"] = pd.to_datetime(merged["stop_s"], unit="s").astype(
+        "datetime64[ns]"
+    )
+    merged["duration"] = (merged["stop_s"] - merged["start_s"]).astype("int64")
+    return merged.loc[:, columns].reset_index(drop=True)
+
+
+def build_overlap_pairs(views_frame, schedule_frame):
+    """Build interval-overlap pairs between view rows and schedule programs.
+
+    Returns a dictionary with positional view and schedule indices, overlap
+    seconds, the number of candidate interval pairs, and a monotonicity flag
+    for schedule end times within each channel.
+    """
+    view = pd.DataFrame({
+        "view_idx": np.arange(len(views_frame), dtype=np.int64),
+        "user_id": views_frame["user_id"].to_numpy(),
+        "channel_id": views_frame["vsetv_id"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
+        "vstart": to_epoch_seconds(views_frame["start_time"]),
+        "view_duration": views_frame["duration"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
+    })
+    view["vend"] = view["vstart"] + view["view_duration"]
+
+    program = pd.DataFrame({
+        "sched_idx": np.arange(len(schedule_frame), dtype=np.int64),
+        "channel_id": schedule_frame["channel_id"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
+        "tv_show_id": schedule_frame["tv_show_id"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
+        "pstart": to_epoch_seconds(schedule_frame["start_time"]),
+        "show_duration": schedule_frame["duration"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
+    })
+    program["pend"] = program["pstart"] + program["show_duration"]
+
+    view = view.sort_values(["channel_id", "vstart"], kind="mergesort").reset_index(drop=True)
+    program = program.sort_values(["channel_id", "pstart"], kind="mergesort").reset_index(drop=True)
+
+    end_monotonic = (
+        program.groupby("channel_id", sort=False)["pend"].diff().fillna(0).ge(0).all()
+    )
+
+    view_channel = view["channel_id"].to_numpy()
+    view_start = view["vstart"].to_numpy()
+    view_end = view["vend"].to_numpy()
+    program_channel = program["channel_id"].to_numpy()
+    program_start = program["pstart"].to_numpy()
+    program_end = program["pend"].to_numpy()
+    program_show = program["tv_show_id"].to_numpy()
+    view_index = view["view_idx"].to_numpy()
+    program_index = program["sched_idx"].to_numpy()
+
+    view_group_start = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, view_channel[1:] != view_channel[:-1]])
+    view_group_end = np.r_[view_group_start[1:], len(view_channel)]
+    program_group_start = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, program_channel[1:] != program_channel[:-1]])
+    program_group_end = np.r_[program_group_start[1:], len(program_channel)]
+    program_group_channel = program_channel[program_group_start]
+
+    view_parts = []
+    program_parts = []
+    overlap_parts = []
+    total_candidates = 0
+
+    for view_begin, view_stop in zip(view_group_start, view_group_end):
+        channel = view_channel[view_begin]
+        program_position = np.searchsorted(program_group_channel, channel)
+        if program_position >= len(program_group_channel):
+            continue
+        if program_group_channel[program_position] != channel:
+            continue
+
+        program_begin = program_group_start[program_position]
+        program_stop = program_group_end[program_position]
+        channel_program_start = program_start[program_begin:program_stop]
+        channel_program_end = program_end[program_begin:program_stop]
+
+        low = np.searchsorted(channel_program_end, view_start[view_begin:view_stop], side="right")
+        high = np.searchsorted(channel_program_start, view_end[view_begin:view_stop], side="left")
+        counts = np.maximum(high - low, 0)
+        total_candidates += int(counts.sum())
+        if counts.sum() == 0:
+            continue
+
+        repeated_view = np.repeat(np.arange(view_stop - view_begin, dtype=np.int64), counts)
+        pair_offsets = np.arange(int(counts.sum()), dtype=np.int64) - np.repeat(
+            np.cumsum(counts) - counts, counts
+        )
+        program_offset = low[repeated_view] + pair_offsets
+
+        overlap_seconds = (
+            np.minimum(view_end[view_begin:view_stop][repeated_view], channel_program_end[program_offset])
+            - np.maximum(view_start[view_begin:view_stop][repeated_view], channel_program_start[program_offset])
+        )
+        keep = (overlap_seconds > 0) & (program_show[program_begin + program_offset] != 0)
+        if not keep.any():
+            continue
+
+        view_parts.append(
+            view_index[view_begin:view_stop][repeated_view[keep]].astype(np.int32)
+        )
+        program_parts.append(
+            program_index[program_begin + program_offset[keep]].astype(np.int32)
+        )
+        overlap_parts.append(overlap_seconds[keep].astype(np.int32))
+
+    if view_parts:
+        pair_view_index = np.concatenate(view_parts)
+        pair_program_index = np.concatenate(program_parts)
+        pair_overlap = np.concatenate(overlap_parts)
+    else:
+        pair_view_index = np.array([], dtype=np.int32)
+        pair_program_index = np.array([], dtype=np.int32)
+        pair_overlap = np.array([], dtype=np.int32)
+
+    return {
+        "view_idx": pair_view_index,
+        "sched_idx": pair_program_index,
+        "overlap_s": pair_overlap,
+        "n_candidates": total_candidates,
+        "end_monotonic": bool(end_monotonic),
+    }
+
+
+def build_airing_table(pair_frame, ratio_threshold=RATIO_THRESHOLD):
+    """Aggregate interval pairs into user-show-airing rows with a ratio flag."""
+    airing = pair_frame.groupby(
+        ["user_id", "tv_show_id", "sched_idx"], sort=False
+    ).agg(
+        watched_s=("overlap_s", "sum"),
+        show_duration=("show_duration", "first"),
+    ).reset_index()
+    airing["ratio"] = (
+        np.minimum(airing["watched_s"], airing["show_duration"])
+        / airing["show_duration"].replace(0, np.nan)
+    )
+    airing["qualified"] = airing["ratio"] >= ratio_threshold
+    return airing
+
+
+def build_aggregated_items(pair_frame, ratio_threshold=RATIO_THRESHOLD):
+    """Build aggregated user-show items and return airing, user-show, and items."""
+    airing = build_airing_table(pair_frame, ratio_threshold=ratio_threshold)
+    user_show = airing.groupby(
+        ["user_id", "tv_show_id"], sort=False
+    ).agg(
+        total_watched_s=("watched_s", "sum"),
+        total_show_duration_s=("show_duration", "sum"),
+        qualified_airings=("qualified", "sum"),
+    ).reset_index()
+    user_show["aggregate_ratio"] = (
+        np.minimum(user_show["total_watched_s"], user_show["total_show_duration_s"])
+        / user_show["total_show_duration_s"].replace(0, np.nan)
+    )
+    user_show["aggregated_qualified"] = user_show["aggregate_ratio"] >= ratio_threshold
+    items = user_show[
+        user_show["aggregated_qualified"] & (user_show["qualified_airings"] >= 1)
+    ].copy()
+    return airing, user_show, items
+
+
+def items_for_weeks(pair_frame, views_frame, week_values, ratio_threshold=RATIO_THRESHOLD):
+    """Filter interval pairs to selected ISO weeks and return aggregated items."""
+    week_values = np.asarray(list(week_values))
+    view_week = views_frame["iso_week"].to_numpy()
+    pair_week = view_week[pair_frame["view_idx"].to_numpy()]
+    mask = np.isin(pair_week, week_values)
+    subset = pair_frame.loc[mask]
+    _, _, items = build_aggregated_items(subset, ratio_threshold=ratio_threshold)
+    return items
+
+
+def items_for_weeks_with_ratio(pair_frame, views_frame, week_values, ratio_threshold):
+    """Return aggregated items for weeks using an explicit ratio threshold."""
+    return items_for_weeks(
+        pair_frame, views_frame, week_values, ratio_threshold=ratio_threshold
+    )
+
+
+def items_for_week_with_ratio(pair_frame, views_frame, week_values, ratio_threshold):
+    """Alias for items_for_weeks_with_ratio kept for the requested API."""
+    return items_for_weeks_with_ratio(
+        pair_frame, views_frame, week_values, ratio_threshold=ratio_threshold
+    )
+
+
+def _views_from_intervals(intervals, user_id=1, vsetv_id=10):
+    """Build a typed view frame from (start, stop) second intervals."""
+    rows = []
+    for start, stop in intervals:
+        rows.append({
+            "user_id": user_id,
+            "vsetv_id": vsetv_id,
+            "start_time": pd.Timestamp("2020-01-01") + pd.Timedelta(seconds=start),
+            "stop_time": pd.Timestamp("2020-01-01") + pd.Timedelta(seconds=stop),
+            "duration": stop - start,
+        })
+    frame = pd.DataFrame(rows)
+    frame["user_id"] = frame["user_id"].astype("uint64")
+    frame["vsetv_id"] = frame["vsetv_id"].astype("int64")
+    frame["start_time"] = frame["start_time"].astype("datetime64[ns]")
+    frame["stop_time"] = frame["stop_time"].astype("datetime64[ns]")
+    frame["duration"] = frame["duration"].astype("int64")
+    return frame
+
+
+@_requires_pytest
+def test_four_identical_intervals_collapse_to_one():
+    """Four copies of one interval must collapse to a single row."""
+    frame = _views_from_intervals([(0, 60)] * 4)
+    merged = merge_overlapping_views(frame)
+    assert merged.shape[0] == 1
+    assert int(merged.loc[0, "duration"]) == 60
+
+
+@_requires_pytest
+def test_two_partially_overlapping_intervals_collapse_to_one():
+    """Two partially overlapping intervals must collapse to one span."""
+    frame = _views_from_intervals([(0, 60), (30, 90)])
+    merged = merge_overlapping_views(frame)
+    assert merged.shape[0] == 1
+    assert int(merged.loc[0, "duration"]) == 90
+
+
+@_requires_pytest
+def test_two_touching_intervals_stay_separate():
+    """Intervals that only touch at an endpoint must stay separate."""
+    frame = _views_from_intervals([(0, 60), (60, 120)])
+    merged = merge_overlapping_views(frame)
+    assert merged.shape[0] == 2
+
+
+@_requires_pytest
+def test_three_disjoint_intervals_stay_separate():
+    """Three disjoint intervals must stay separate."""
+    frame = _views_from_intervals([(0, 10), (20, 30), (40, 50)])
+    merged = merge_overlapping_views(frame)
+    assert merged.shape[0] == 3
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    test_four_identical_intervals_collapse_to_one()
+    test_two_partially_overlapping_intervals_collapse_to_one()
+    test_two_touching_intervals_stay_separate()
+    test_three_disjoint_intervals_stay_separate()
+    print("src/data.py self-tests passed")

## D. Join quality and interaction definition

===== CELL 33 markdown =====
A view and a program are joined when channel_id equals vsetv_id and their time intervals overlap. The overlap is computed in integer seconds: overlap_s = max(0, min(view_end, program_end) - max(view_start, program_start)). The threshold overlap_s / duration_show >= 0.8 is the rule described for the target labeling; it is shown as a candidate threshold and is not treated as an optimized parameter.

===== CELL 34 code =====
def build_overlap_pairs(views_frame, schedule_frame):
    view = pd.DataFrame({
        "view_idx": np.arange(len(views_frame), dtype=np.int64),
        "user_id": views_frame["user_id"].to_numpy(),
        "channel_id": views_frame["vsetv_id"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
        "vstart": to_epoch_seconds(views_frame["start_time"]),
        "view_duration": views_frame["duration"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
    })
    view["vend"] = view["vstart"] + view["view_duration"]

    program = pd.DataFrame({
        "sched_idx": np.arange(len(schedule_frame), dtype=np.int64),
        "channel_id": schedule_frame["channel_id"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
        "tv_show_id": schedule_frame["tv_show_id"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
        "pstart": to_epoch_seconds(schedule_frame["start_time"]),
        "show_duration": schedule_frame["duration"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
    })
    program["pend"] = program["pstart"] + program["show_duration"]

    view = view.sort_values(["channel_id", "vstart"], kind="mergesort").reset_index(drop=True)
    program = program.sort_values(["channel_id", "pstart"], kind="mergesort").reset_index(drop=True)

    end_monotonic = (
        program.groupby("channel_id", sort=False)["pend"].diff().fillna(0).ge(0).all()
    )
    print("Schedule end-time nondecreasing within each channel:", bool(end_monotonic))

    view_channel = view["channel_id"].to_numpy()
    view_start = view["vstart"].to_numpy()
    view_end = view["vend"].to_numpy()
    program_channel = program["channel_id"].to_numpy()
    program_start = program["pstart"].to_numpy()
    program_end = program["pend"].to_numpy()
    program_show = program["tv_show_id"].to_numpy()
    view_index = view["view_idx"].to_numpy()
    program_index = program["sched_idx"].to_numpy()

    view_group_start = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, view_channel[1:] != view_channel[:-1]])
    view_group_end = np.r_[view_group_start[1:], len(view_channel)]
    program_group_start = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, program_channel[1:] != program_channel[:-1]])
    program_group_end = np.r_[program_group_start[1:], len(program_channel)]
    program_group_channel = program_channel[program_group_start]

    view_parts = []
    program_parts = []
    overlap_parts = []
    total_candidates = 0

    for view_begin, view_stop in zip(view_group_start, view_group_end):
        channel = view_channel[view_begin]
        program_position = np.searchsorted(program_group_channel, channel)
        if program_position >= len(program_group_channel):
            continue
        if program_group_channel[program_position] != channel:
            continue

        program_begin = program_group_start[program_position]
        program_stop = program_group_end[program_position]
        channel_program_start = program_start[program_begin:program_stop]
        channel_program_end = program_end[program_begin:program_stop]

        low = np.searchsorted(channel_program_end, view_start[view_begin:view_stop], side="right")
        high = np.searchsorted(channel_program_start, view_end[view_begin:view_stop], side="left")
        counts = np.maximum(high - low, 0)
        total_candidates += int(counts.sum())
        if counts.sum() == 0:
            continue

        repeated_view = np.repeat(np.arange(view_stop - view_begin, dtype=np.int64), counts)
        pair_offsets = np.arange(int(counts.sum()), dtype=np.int64) - np.repeat(
            np.cumsum(counts) - counts, counts
        )
        program_offset = low[repeated_view] + pair_offsets

        overlap_seconds = (
            np.minimum(view_end[view_begin:view_stop][repeated_view], channel_program_end[program_offset])
            - np.maximum(view_start[view_begin:view_stop][repeated_view], channel_program_start[program_offset])
        )
        keep = (overlap_seconds > 0) & (program_show[program_begin + program_offset] != 0)
        if not keep.any():
            continue

        view_parts.append(
            view_index[view_begin:view_stop][repeated_view[keep]].astype(np.int32)
        )
        program_parts.append(
            program_index[program_begin + program_offset[keep]].astype(np.int32)
        )
        overlap_parts.append(overlap_seconds[keep].astype(np.int32))

    if view_parts:
        pair_view_index = np.concatenate(view_parts)
        pair_program_index = np.concatenate(program_parts)
        pair_overlap = np.concatenate(overlap_parts)
    else:
        pair_view_index = np.array([], dtype=np.int32)
        pair_program_index = np.array([], dtype=np.int32)
        pair_overlap = np.array([], dtype=np.int32)

    return {
        "view_idx": pair_view_index,
        "sched_idx": pair_program_index,
        "overlap_s": pair_overlap,
        "n_candidates": total_candidates,
    }


def build_airing_table(pair_frame, ratio_threshold=0.8):
    airing = pair_frame.groupby(
        ["user_id", "tv_show_id", "sched_idx"], sort=False
    ).agg(
        watched_s=("overlap_s", "sum"),
        show_duration=("show_duration", "first"),
    ).reset_index()
    airing["ratio"] = (
        np.minimum(airing["watched_s"], airing["show_duration"])
        / airing["show_duration"].replace(0, np.nan)
    )
    airing["qualified"] = airing["ratio"] >= ratio_threshold
    return airing


def build_aggregated_items(pair_frame, ratio_threshold=0.8):
    airing = build_airing_table(pair_frame, ratio_threshold=ratio_threshold)
    user_show = airing.groupby(
        ["user_id", "tv_show_id"], sort=False
    ).agg(
        total_watched_s=("watched_s", "sum"),
        total_show_duration_s=("show_duration", "sum"),
        qualified_airings=("qualified", "sum"),
    ).reset_index()
    user_show["aggregate_ratio"] = (
        np.minimum(user_show["total_watched_s"], user_show["total_show_duration_s"])
        / user_show["total_show_duration_s"].replace(0, np.nan)
    )
    user_show["aggregated_qualified"] = user_show["aggregate_ratio"] >= ratio_threshold
    items = user_show[
        user_show["aggregated_qualified"] & (user_show["qualified_airings"] >= 1)
    ].copy()
    return airing, user_show, items


def items_for_weeks(pair_frame, views_frame, week_values):
    week_values = np.asarray(list(week_values))
    view_week = views_frame["iso_week"].to_numpy()
    pair_week = view_week[pair_frame["view_idx"].to_numpy()]
    mask = np.isin(pair_week, week_values)
    subset = pair_frame.loc[mask]
    _, _, items = build_aggregated_items(subset, ratio_threshold=0.8)
    return items

def apply_threshold(frame, spec):
    if spec["kind"] == "overlap_s":
        mask = frame["overlap_s"] > spec["value"] if spec["strict"] else frame["overlap_s"] >= spec["value"]
    elif spec["kind"] == "view_ratio":
        mask = frame["overlap_s"] / frame["view_duration"].replace(0, np.nan) >= spec["value"]
    elif spec["kind"] == "show_ratio":
        mask = frame["overlap_s"] / frame["show_duration"].replace(0, np.nan) >= spec["value"]
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown threshold kind: {spec['kind']}")
    return mask.fillna(False)

Candidate “view × program” pairs: 7.75 million, of which 3.85 million pairs have a positive time overlap and tv_show_id ≠ 0, covering 4,895 users, 4,363 shows, and 2.96 million unique views. The overlaps are also heavy‑tailed: the median is ~523 s, with a maximum of 30,000 s.

 When the threshold is tightened, the sample collapses very aggressively. That is, the relative threshold based on program duration is significantly stricter than the absolute threshold based on seconds, and it is this threshold that determines what proportion of shows we consider “watched.”

After transitioning to the "broadcast" level (aggregation by user_id, tv_show_id, sched_idx), 3.01 million rows remain, of which 616,000 are qualified. def average_precision_at_k(recommended, relevant, k=5):
    relevant = set(relevant)
    if not relevant:
        return np.nan
    recommended = list(recommended)[:k]
    hits = 0
    precision_sum = 0.0
    for rank, item in enumerate(recommended, start=1):
        if item in relevant:
            hits += 1
            precision_sum += hits / rank
    return precision_sum / min(len(relevant), k)

def apply_threshold(frame, spec):
    if spec["kind"] == "overlap_s":
        mask = frame["overlap_s"] > spec["value"] if spec["strict"] else frame["overlap_s"] >= spec["value"]
    elif spec["kind"] == "view_ratio":
        mask = frame["overlap_s"] / frame["view_duration"].replace(0, np.nan) >= spec["value"]
    elif spec["kind"] == "show_ratio":
        mask = frame["overlap_s"] / frame["show_duration"].replace(0, np.nan) >= spec["value"]
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown threshold kind: {spec['kind']}")
    return mask.fillna(False)

def average_precision_at_k(recommended, relevant, k=5):
    relevant = set(relevant)
    if not relevant:
        return np.nan
    recommended = list(recommended)[:k]
    hits = 0
    precision_sum = 0.0
    for rank, item in enumerate(recommended, start=1):
        if item in relevant:
            hits += 1
            precision_sum += hits / rank
    return precision_sum / min(len(relevant), k)

### Conclusion
Validation is constructed correctly with respect to leakage: the training window is weeks 11–20, the target window is 21–30, and evaluation is restricted to test users who have at least one aggregated-rule item in the target window; there are 1,214 such users out of 1,260. For these users, the median number of target items is 11, the 95th percentile is 98, and the maximum is 250, so it is useful to consider the metric together with recall and NDCG, rather than AP@5 alone. Among the three simple baselines, global popularity over weeks 11–20 yields MAP@5 = 0.055459, recent popularity over weeks 17–20 yields 0.078839, and personal history over 11–20 yields 0.078950. Thus, recent popularity improves global popularity by about 42%, whereas personal history by itself barely outperforms recent popularity, and for 23 users its recommendations are empty, yielding AP = 0. The AP@5 unit test passed correctly: the value 0.555556 matched the expected value, which confirms that the metric is implemented correctly, although it does not guarantee that this is a sufficient sole quality metric.

## Notes and caveats

- The training view log contains rows for ISO weeks 11-30 only; no view rows exist for ISO weeks 31-42.
- The view log contains playback rows only; there is no explicit negative feedback signal.
- View durations vary from seconds to more than a day, so any interaction definition that uses watched time needs normalization by program duration.
- The schedule files use tv_show_id = 0 for a large fraction of rows; these rows are excluded from the item catalogue and from category and genre distributions.
- Observed user_id values exceed the signed int64 maximum, so user_id is stored as uint64.
- Schedule exports overlap at file boundaries in calendar time: ISO weeks 21 and 31 appear in two files. Exact duplicate rows on (channel_id, start_time) are removed before schedule-level charts and before the training join; after deduplication 1 row was removed, so the intersection by exact keys is negligible.
- Schedule end times are nondecreasing within each channel in the observed training data; a small number of adjacent rows have start_time earlier than the previous row end_time.
- Text columns contain valid Unicode Cyrillic in the observed files; the mojibake check did not detect a reversed-encoding pattern requiring conversion.
- The submission file has 1260 unique user_id values and a tv_show_id column with five space-separated placeholder slots per row; all observed slots are 0.
- The public and private test parts are split by user, nominally 50/50, not by time.
- The test schedule covers ISO weeks 31-42 and is used here only as a reference for which tv_show_id values exist.
- The validation target window 21-30 is used only for baseline evaluation; all three reference baselines are constructed from weeks 11-20 only.

### Conclusion
The log contains 4,914 unique users and 202 unique channels over 20 ISO weeks. The distribution of view duration is heavily skewed to the right: median 396 s (~6.6 min), mean ~1,480 s, p99 ~14,079 s (~4 h), maximum ~342,145 s (~95 h). There are no rows with duration ≤ 0, but ~0.96% of views longer than 4 hours are clear outliers that should either be trimmed or filtered during modeling. The peak activity is at 21:00, and by day of the week it’s Sunday. The log volume drops from ~400–465 thousand lines/week (weeks 11–18) to ~105–280 thousand (weeks 19–30); in weeks 28–30 there is a rebound; its cause is unknown. Candidate hypotheses: change in the logging window, seasonality, delayed event catch-up. Requires verification (by minute/device) before drawing conclusions. The distribution of views per user and per channel has a long tail (median: 874 lines per user, 5,901 per channel), which is expected for the TV domain.

def fix_mojibake(text):
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return text
    try:
        return text.encode("cp1251").decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    except Exception:
        return text


def has_mojibake(text):
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        return False
    if "\ufffd" in text or "??????" in text:
        return True
    markers = [
        "\u0420\u00b0", "\u0420\u00b5", "\u0420\u00bb", "\u0420\u00be",
        "\u0421\u0402", "\u0421\u201a", "\u0421\u0453", "\u0432\u0402",
    ]
    return any(marker in text for marker in markers)

### Conclusion
The log contains 4,914 unique users and 202 unique channels over 20 ISO weeks. The distribution of view duration is heavily skewed to the right: median 396 s (~6.6 min), mean ~1,480 s, p99 ~14,079 s (~4 h), maximum ~342,145 s (~95 h). There are no rows with duration ≤ 0, but ~0.96% of views longer than 4 hours are clear outliers that should either be trimmed or filtered during modeling. The peak activity is at 21:00, and by day of the week it’s Sunday. The log volume drops from ~400–465 thousand lines/week (weeks 11–18) to ~105–280 thousand (weeks 19–30); in weeks 28–30 there is a rebound; its cause is unknown. Candidate hypotheses: change in the logging window, seasonality, delayed event catch-up. Requires verification (by minute/device) before drawing conclusions. The distribution of views per user and per channel has a long tail (median: 874 lines per user, 5,901 per channel), which is expected for the TV domain.

"""Reusable data helpers for the sweet.tv recommender project."""

import unittest

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

RATIO_THRESHOLD = 0.8

try:
    import pytest
except ImportError:
    pytest = None

_requires_pytest = (
    unittest.skip("pytest is not installed") if pytest is None else (lambda func: func)
)


def to_epoch_seconds(series):
    """Convert a datetime-like Series to integer Unix seconds."""
    return series.astype("datetime64[ns]").astype("int64") // 10**9


def merge_overlapping_views(views_df):
    """Merge overlapping view intervals for each (user_id, vsetv_id) pair.

    Intervals are sorted by start time and merged when the next start is
    strictly earlier than the running maximum stop. Intervals that only touch
    at an endpoint are kept separate. The returned duration is the merged
    interval length in seconds.
    """
    columns = ["user_id", "vsetv_id", "start_time", "stop_time", "duration"]
    missing = [column for column in columns if column not in views_df.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing required view columns: {missing}")

    if views_df.shape[0] == 0:
        empty = views_df.loc[:, columns].copy()
        empty["user_id"] = empty["user_id"].astype("uint64")
        empty["vsetv_id"] = empty["vsetv_id"].astype("int64")
        empty["start_time"] = empty["start_time"].astype("datetime64[ns]")
        empty["stop_time"] = empty["stop_time"].astype("datetime64[ns]")
        empty["duration"] = empty["duration"].astype("int64")
        return empty.reset_index(drop=True)

    frame = views_df.loc[:, ["user_id", "vsetv_id", "start_time", "stop_time"]].copy()
    frame["start_s"] = to_epoch_seconds(frame["start_time"])
    frame["stop_s"] = to_epoch_seconds(frame["stop_time"])
    frame = frame.sort_values(
        ["user_id", "vsetv_id", "start_s", "stop_s"], kind="mergesort"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    keys = ["user_id", "vsetv_id"]
    previous_max_stop = frame.groupby(keys, sort=False)["stop_s"].cummax().shift(1)
    group_change = (
        frame["user_id"].ne(frame["user_id"].shift())
        | frame["vsetv_id"].ne(frame["vsetv_id"].shift())
    )
    new_segment = group_change | frame["start_s"].ge(previous_max_stop)
    segment_id = new_segment.cumsum()

    merged = frame.groupby("segment_id", sort=False).agg(
        user_id=("user_id", "first"),
        vsetv_id=("vsetv_id", "first"),
        start_s=("start_s", "min"),
        stop_s=("stop_s", "max"),
    ).reset_index(drop=True)

    merged["start_time"] = pd.to_datetime(merged["start_s"], unit="s").astype(
        "datetime64[ns]"
    )
    merged["stop_time"] = pd.to_datetime(merged["stop_s"], unit="s").astype(
        "datetime64[ns]"
    )
    merged["duration"] = (merged["stop_s"] - merged["start_s"]).astype("int64")
    return merged.loc[:, columns].reset_index(drop=True)


def build_overlap_pairs(views_frame, schedule_frame):
    """Build interval-overlap pairs between view rows and schedule programs.

    Returns a dictionary with positional view and schedule indices, overlap
    seconds, the number of candidate interval pairs, and a monotonicity flag
    for schedule end times within each channel.
    """
    view = pd.DataFrame({
        "view_idx": np.arange(len(views_frame), dtype=np.int64),
        "user_id": views_frame["user_id"].to_numpy(),
        "channel_id": views_frame["vsetv_id"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
        "vstart": to_epoch_seconds(views_frame["start_time"]),
        "view_duration": views_frame["duration"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
    })
    view["vend"] = view["vstart"] + view["view_duration"]

    program = pd.DataFrame({
        "sched_idx": np.arange(len(schedule_frame), dtype=np.int64),
        "channel_id": schedule_frame["channel_id"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
        "tv_show_id": schedule_frame["tv_show_id"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
        "pstart": to_epoch_seconds(schedule_frame["start_time"]),
        "show_duration": schedule_frame["duration"].to_numpy().astype(np.int64),
    })
    program["pend"] = program["pstart"] + program["show_duration"]

    view = view.sort_values(["channel_id", "vstart"], kind="mergesort").reset_index(drop=True)
    program = program.sort_values(["channel_id", "pstart"], kind="mergesort").reset_index(drop=True)

    end_monotonic = (
        program.groupby("channel_id", sort=False)["pend"].diff().fillna(0).ge(0).all()
    )

    view_channel = view["channel_id"].to_numpy()
    view_start = view["vstart"].to_numpy()
    view_end = view["vend"].to_numpy()
    program_channel = program["channel_id"].to_numpy()
    program_start = program["pstart"].to_numpy()
    program_end = program["pend"].to_numpy()
    program_show = program["tv_show_id"].to_numpy()
    view_index = view["view_idx"].to_numpy()
    program_index = program["sched_idx"].to_numpy()

    view_group_start = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, view_channel[1:] != view_channel[:-1]])
    view_group_end = np.r_[view_group_start[1:], len(view_channel)]
    program_group_start = np.flatnonzero(np.r_[True, program_channel[1:] != program_channel[:-1]])
    program_group_end = np.r_[program_group_start[1:], len(program_channel)]
    program_group_channel = program_channel[program_group_start]

    view_parts = []
    program_parts = []
    overlap_parts = []
    total_candidates = 0

    for view_begin, view_stop in zip(view_group_start, view_group_end):
        channel = view_channel[view_begin]
        program_position = np.searchsorted(program_group_channel, channel)
        if program_position >= len(program_group_channel):
            continue
        if program_group_channel[program_position] != channel:
            continue

        program_begin = program_group_start[program_position]
        program_stop = program_group_end[program_position]
        channel_program_start = program_start[program_begin:program_stop]
        channel_program_end = program_end[program_begin:program_stop]

        low = np.searchsorted(channel_program_end, view_start[view_begin:view_stop], side="right")
        high = np.searchsorted(channel_program_start, view_end[view_begin:view_stop], side="left")
        counts = np.maximum(high - low, 0)
        total_candidates += int(counts.sum())
        if counts.sum() == 0:
            continue

        repeated_view = np.repeat(np.arange(view_stop - view_begin, dtype=np.int64), counts)
        pair_offsets = np.arange(int(counts.sum()), dtype=np.int64) - np.repeat(
            np.cumsum(counts) - counts, counts
        )
        program_offset = low[repeated_view] + pair_offsets

        overlap_seconds = (
            np.minimum(view_end[view_begin:view_stop][repeated_view], channel_program_end[program_offset])
            - np.maximum(view_start[view_begin:view_stop][repeated_view], channel_program_start[program_offset])
        )
        keep = (overlap_seconds > 0) & (program_show[program_begin + program_offset] != 0)
        if not keep.any():
            continue

        view_parts.append(
            view_index[view_begin:view_stop][repeated_view[keep]].astype(np.int32)
        )
        program_parts.append(
            program_index[program_begin + program_offset[keep]].astype(np.int32)
        )
        overlap_parts.append(overlap_seconds[keep].astype(np.int32))

    if view_parts:
        pair_view_index = np.concatenate(view_parts)
        pair_program_index = np.concatenate(program_parts)
        pair_overlap = np.concatenate(overlap_parts)
    else:
        pair_view_index = np.array([], dtype=np.int32)
        pair_program_index = np.array([], dtype=np.int32)
        pair_overlap = np.array([], dtype=np.int32)

    return {
        "view_idx": pair_view_index,
        "sched_idx": pair_program_index,
        "overlap_s": pair_overlap,
        "n_candidates": total_candidates,
        "end_monotonic": bool(end_monotonic),
    }


def build_airing_table(pair_frame, ratio_threshold=RATIO_THRESHOLD):
    """Aggregate interval pairs into user-show-airing rows with a ratio flag."""
    airing = pair_frame.groupby(
        ["user_id", "tv_show_id", "sched_idx"], sort=False
    ).agg(
        watched_s=("overlap_s", "sum"),
        show_duration=("show_duration", "first"),
    ).reset_index()
    airing["ratio"] = (
        np.minimum(airing["watched_s"], airing["show_duration"])
        / airing["show_duration"].replace(0, np.nan)
    )
    airing["qualified"] = airing["ratio"] >= ratio_threshold
    return airing


def build_aggregated_items(pair_frame, ratio_threshold=RATIO_THRESHOLD):
    """Build aggregated user-show items and return airing, user-show, and items."""
    airing = build_airing_table(pair_frame, ratio_threshold=ratio_threshold)
    user_show = airing.groupby(
        ["user_id", "tv_show_id"], sort=False
    ).agg(
        total_watched_s=("watched_s", "sum"),
        total_show_duration_s=("show_duration", "sum"),
        qualified_airings=("qualified", "sum"),
    ).reset_index()
    user_show["aggregate_ratio"] = (
        np.minimum(user_show["total_watched_s"], user_show["total_show_duration_s"])
        / user_show["total_show_duration_s"].replace(0, np.nan)
    )
    user_show["aggregated_qualified"] = user_show["aggregate_ratio"] >= ratio_threshold
    items = user_show[
        user_show["aggregated_qualified"] & (user_show["qualified_airings"] >= 1)
    ].copy()
    return airing, user_show, items


def items_for_weeks(pair_frame, views_frame, week_values, ratio_threshold=RATIO_THRESHOLD):
    """Filter interval pairs to selected ISO weeks and return aggregated items."""
    week_values = np.asarray(list(week_values))
    view_week = views_frame["iso_week"].to_numpy()
    pair_week = view_week[pair_frame["view_idx"].to_numpy()]
    mask = np.isin(pair_week, week_values)
    subset = pair_frame.loc[mask]
    _, _, items = build_aggregated_items(subset, ratio_threshold=ratio_threshold)
    return items


def items_for_weeks_with_ratio(pair_frame, views_frame, week_values, ratio_threshold):
    """Return aggregated items for weeks using an explicit ratio threshold."""
    return items_for_weeks(
        pair_frame, views_frame, week_values, ratio_threshold=ratio_threshold
    )


def items_for_week_with_ratio(pair_frame, views_frame, week_values, ratio_threshold):
    """Alias for items_for_weeks_with_ratio kept for the requested API."""
    return items_for_weeks_with_ratio(
        pair_frame, views_frame, week_values, ratio_threshold=ratio_threshold
    )


def _views_from_intervals(intervals, user_id=1, vsetv_id=10):
    rows = []
    for start, stop in intervals:
        rows.append({
            "user_id": user_id,
            "vsetv_id": vsetv_id,
            "start_time": pd.Timestamp("2020-01-01") + pd.Timedelta(seconds=start),
            "stop_time": pd.Timestamp("2020-01-01") + pd.Timedelta(seconds=stop),
            "duration": stop - start,
        })
    frame = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    frame["user_id"] = frame["user_id"].astype("uint64")
    frame["vsetv_id"] = frame["vsetv_id"].astype("int64")
    frame["start_time"] = frame["start_time"].astype("datetime64[ns]")
    frame["stop_time"] = frame["stop_time"].astype("datetime64[ns]")
    frame["duration"] = frame["duration"].astype("int64")
    return frame


@_requires_pytest
def test_four_identical_intervals_collapse_to_one():
    """Four copies of one interval must collapse to a single row."""
    frame = _views_from_intervals([(0, 60)] * 4)
    merged = merge_overlapping_views(frame)
    assert merged.shape[0] == 1
    assert int(merged.loc[0, "duration"]) == 60


@_requires_pytest
def test_two_partially_overlapping_intervals_collapse_to_one():
    """Two partially overlapping intervals must collapse to one span."""
    frame = _views_from_intervals([(0, 60), (30, 90)])
    merged = merge_overlapping_views(frame)
    assert merged.shape[0] == 1
    assert int(merged.loc[0, "duration"]) == 90


@_requires_pytest
def test_two_touching_intervals_stay_separate():
    """Intervals that only touch at an endpoint must stay separate."""
    frame = _views_from_intervals([(0, 60), (60, 120)])
    merged = merge_overlapping_views(frame)
    assert merged.shape[0] == 2


@_requires_pytest
def test_three_disjoint_intervals_stay_separate():
    """Three disjoint intervals must stay separate."""
    frame = _views_from_intervals([(0, 10), (20, 30), (40, 50)])
    merged = merge_overlapping_views(frame)
    assert merged.shape[0] == 3


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_four_identical_intervals_collapse_to_one()
    test_two_partially_overlapping_intervals_collapse_to_one()
    test_two_touching_intervals_stay_separate()
    test_three_disjoint_intervals_stay_separate()
    print("src/data.py self-tests passed")

def load_view_log(path):
    frame = pd.read_parquet(path)
    frame = frame.rename(columns={"duraton": "duration", "end_time": "stop_time"})
    if "duration" not in frame.columns:
        raise ValueError("View log has neither duraton nor duration column")
    frame["user_id"] = frame["user_id"].astype("uint64")
    frame["vsetv_id"] = frame["vsetv_id"].astype("int64")
    frame["start_time"] = pd.to_datetime(frame["start_time"], errors="coerce").astype("datetime64[ns]")
    if "stop_time" in frame.columns:
        frame["stop_time"] = pd.to_datetime(frame["stop_time"], errors="coerce").astype("datetime64[ns]")
    else:
        frame["stop_time"] = frame["start_time"] + pd.to_timedelta(frame["duration"], unit="s")
    frame["duration"] = pd.to_numeric(frame["duration"], errors="coerce").fillna(0).astype("int64")
    return frame

def load_view_log(path):
    frame = pd.read_parquet(path)
    frame = frame.rename(columns={"duraton": "duration", "end_time": "stop_time"})
    if "duration" not in frame.columns:
        raise ValueError("View log has neither duraton nor duration column")
    frame["user_id"] = frame["user_id"].astype("uint64")
    frame["vsetv_id"] = frame["vsetv_id"].astype("int64")
    frame["start_time"] = pd.to_datetime(frame["start_time"], errors="coerce").astype("datetime64[ns]")
    if "stop_time" in frame.columns:
        frame["stop_time"] = pd.to_datetime(frame["stop_time"], errors="coerce").astype("datetime64[ns]")
    else:
        frame["stop_time"] = frame["start_time"] + pd.to_timedelta(frame["duration"], unit="s")
    frame["duration"] = pd.to_numeric(frame["duration"], errors="coerce").fillna(0).astype("int64")
    return frame

)

cells.append(new_code_cell('''def ap_at_k(recommended, relevant, k=5):
    """Return AP@k for one user without side effects."""
    relevant = set(relevant)
    if not relevant:
        return np.nan
    hits = 0
    score = 0.0
    for rank, item in enumerate(list(recommended)[:k], start=1):
        if item in relevant:
            hits += 1
            score += hits / rank
    return score / min(len(relevant), k)


def map_at_k(recommendations, ground_truth, k=5):
    """Return MAP@k and the number of users with non-empty ground truth."""
    scores = []
    n_users_eval = 0
    for user, relevant in ground_truth.items():
        if not relevant:
            continue
        n_users_eval += 1
        scores.append(ap_at_k(recommendations.get(user, []), relevant, k=k))
    mean_score = float(np.mean(scores)) if scores else float("nan")
    return mean_score, n_users_eval

cells.append(new_markdown_cell('''## Unified fallback

The same fallback is used for every method: the global top-5 by history popularity, filtered by the candidate pool. A method-specific or empty fallback would make AP = 0 for personal history an artifact of the method rather than a property of the data. If history popularity has fewer than five candidate items, the fallback is deterministically padded from the candidate pool so every recommendation contains exactly five unique ids.'''))

cells.append(new_code_cell('''def fill_with_fallback(recommendations, fallback, k=5):
    """Fill recommendations to exactly k unique ids using the fallback list."""
    result = []
    seen = set()
    for item in list(recommendations) + list(fallback):
        item = int(item)
        if item in seen:
            continue
        result.append(item)
        seen.add(item)
        if len(result) == k:
            break
    return result


def build_fallback(history_items, candidates, k=5):
    """Build a global popularity fallback restricted to candidate show ids."""
    history_pool = history_items[history_items["tv_show_id"].isin(candidates)]
    popularity = history_pool.groupby("tv_show_id")["user_id"].nunique().sort_values(
        ascending=False
    )
    fallback = [int(value) for value in popularity.head(k).index]
    if len(fallback) < k:
        seen = set(fallback)
        extras = [int(value) for value in sorted(candidates) if int(value) not in seen]
        fallback.extend(extras[: k - len(fallback)])
    return fallback

del overlap_arrays, pair_view_index, pair_program_index, pair_overlap
gc.collect()
print("Positive-overlap pairs:", int(pair.shape[0]))
print("Pair build elapsed seconds:", round(time.time() - started, 2))'''))

cells.append(new_markdown_cell('''## Candidate pool and ground truth

The candidate pool is taken from train_schedule_2 because the test candidate space will be limited by the test schedule. Without this restriction, baselines can recommend shows that do not air in the target window and MAP is distorted. The ground truth contains aggregated-rule items for weeks 21-30 that belong to the candidate pool; users with no such items are excluded from the metric.'''))

cells.append(new_code_cell('''candidate_pool = np.unique(
    train_sched_2.loc[train_sched_2["tv_show_id"] != 0, "tv_show_id"].to_numpy()
)
candidate_set = set(int(value) for value in candidate_pool)
print("Candidate pool size:", len(candidate_set))

val_hist = items_for_weeks_with_ratio(
    pair, views_merged, range(11, 21), RATIO_THRESHOLD
)
val_tgt = items_for_weeks_with_ratio(
    pair, views_merged, range(21, 31), RATIO_THRESHOLD
)
val_tgt = val_tgt[val_tgt["tv_show_id"].isin(candidate_set)].copy()

gt_by_user = {
    int(user): set(int(show) for show in group["tv_show_id"])
    for user, group in val_tgt.groupby("user_id", sort=False)
}
gt_sizes = np.array([len(relevant) for relevant in gt_by_user.values()], dtype=np.int64)
print("History items:", int(val_hist.shape[0]))
print("Target items after candidate filter:", int(val_tgt.shape[0]))
print("Users with non-empty target:", int(len(gt_by_user)))
print("Mean target size:", round(float(gt_sizes.mean()), 4) if len(gt_sizes) else 0.0)

del train_sched_core, train_sched_2, schedule_11_30
gc.collect()'''))

cells.append(new_markdown_cell('''## MAP@5 helper

AP@5 = sum over ranks i where the item is relevant of (hits so far / i), divided by min(|target|, 5). MAP@5 is the mean AP@5 over users with non-empty target sets. Users with an empty target set are skipped and are not part of n_users_eval.'''))

cells.append(new_code_cell('''def ap_at_k(recommended, relevant, k=5):
    """Return AP@k for one user without side effects."""
    relevant = set(relevant)
    if not relevant:
        return np.nan
    hits = 0
    score = 0.0
    for rank, item in enumerate(list(recommended)[:k], start=1):
        if item in relevant:
            hits += 1
            score += hits / rank
    return score / min(len(relevant), k)


def map_at_k(recommendations, ground_truth, k=5):
    """Return MAP@k and the number of users with non-empty ground truth."""
    scores = []
    n_users_eval = 0
    for user, relevant in ground_truth.items():
        if not relevant:
            continue
        n_users_eval += 1
        scores.append(ap_at_k(recommendations.get(user, []), relevant, k=k))
    mean_score = float(np.mean(scores)) if scores else float("nan")
    return mean_score, n_users_eval


toy_score = ap_at_k([101, 102, 103, 104, 105], {101, 103, 106}, k=5)
toy_expected = (1 / 1 + 2 / 3) / 3
assert np.isclose(toy_score, toy_expected)
print("AP@5 toy check:", round(float(toy_score), 6), "expected:", round(float(toy_expected), 6))'''))

cells.append(new_markdown_cell('''## Unified fallback

The same fallback is used for every method: the global top-5 by history popularity, filtered by the candidate pool. A method-specific or empty fallback would make AP = 0 for personal history an artifact of the method rather than a property of the data. If history popularity has fewer than five candidate items, the fallback is deterministically padded from the candidate pool so every recommendation contains exactly five unique ids.'''))

cells.append(new_code_cell('''def fill_with_fallback(recommendations, fallback, k=5):
    """Fill recommendations to exactly k unique ids using the fallback list."""
    result = []
    seen = set()
    for item in list(recommendations) + list(fallback):
        item = int(item)
        if item in seen:
            continue
        result.append(item)
        seen.add(item)
        if len(result) == k:
            break
    return result


def build_fallback(history_items, candidates, k=5):
    """Build a global popularity fallback restricted to candidate show ids."""
    history_pool = history_items[history_items["tv_show_id"].isin(candidates)]
    popularity = history_pool.groupby("tv_show_id")["user_id"].nunique().sort_values(
        ascending=False
    )
    fallback = [int(value) for value in popularity.head(k).index]
    if len(fallback) < k:
        seen = set(fallback)
        extras = [int(value) for value in sorted(candidates) if int(value) not in seen]
        fallback.extend(extras[: k - len(fallback)])
    return fallback


global_top5 = build_fallback(val_hist, candidate_set, k=5)
print("Global popularity top-5:", global_top5)
print("Fallback length:", len(global_top5))'''))

cells.append(new_markdown_cell('''## Baselines

All three baselines return exactly five candidate ids and use the same fallback.

- global_pop: top-5 shows by unique users in weeks 11-20, filtered by the candidate pool.
- recent_pop: top-5 shows by unique users in weeks 17-20, filtered by the candidate pool.
- personal: top-5 shows by total_watched_s in weeks 11-20, filtered by the candidate pool, then filled with the fallback.'''))

cells.append(new_code_cell('''recent_hist = items_for_weeks_with_ratio(
    pair, views_merged, range(17, 21), RATIO_THRESHOLD
)
recent_top5 = build_fallback(recent_hist, candidate_set, k=5)

personal_history = val_hist[val_hist["tv_show_id"].isin(candidate_set)].sort_values(
    ["user_id", "total_watched_s", "tv_show_id"],
    ascending=[True, False, True],
)
personal_raw = {
    int(user): [int(show) for show in group["tv_show_id"].head(5)]
    for user, group in personal_history.groupby("user_id", sort=False)
}

global_recs = {
    int(user): fill_with_fallback([], global_top5, k=5)
    for user in gt_by_user
}
recent_recs = {
    int(user): fill_with_fallback([], recent_top5, k=5)
    for user in gt_by_user
}
personal_recs = {
    int(user): fill_with_fallback(personal_raw.get(int(user), []), global_top5, k=5)
    for user in gt_by_user
}

for name, recommendation_map in [
    ("global_pop", global_recs),
    ("recent_pop", recent_recs),
    ("personal", personal_recs),
]:
    assert all(len(recommendation_map[user]) == 5 for user in gt_by_user), name

metric_rows = []
for method, recommendation_map in [
    ("global_pop", global_recs),
    ("recent_pop", recent_recs),
    ("personal", personal_recs),
]:
    mean_score, n_users_eval = map_at_k(recommendation_map, gt_by_user, k=5)
    metric_rows.append({
        "method": method,
        "map_at_5": float(mean_score),
        "n_users_eval": int(n_users_eval),
    })

eval_metrics = pd.DataFrame(metric_rows)
display(eval_metrics)
with open(EVAL_DIR / "eval_metrics.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    json.dump(metric_rows, file, indent=2)
print("Saved:", EVAL_DIR / "eval_metrics.json")
print("Recent popularity top-5:", recent_top5)'''))

cells.append(new_markdown_cell('''## Sensitivity to target threshold

The 0.8 target threshold is a task hyperparameter, not a rule stated in the competition. It leaves a substantially smaller item set than 0.3 or 0.5. The personal baseline is recomputed for thresholds 0.3, 0.5, and 0.8, with the history and fallback rebuilt inside each iteration.'''))

cells.append(new_code_cell('''sensitivity_rows = []
for threshold in [0.3, 0.5, 0.8]:
    hist_t = items_for_weeks_with_ratio(
        pair, views_merged, range(11, 21), threshold
    )
    tgt_t = items_for_weeks_with_ratio(
        pair, views_merged, range(21, 31), threshold
    )
    tgt_t = tgt_t[tgt_t["tv_show_id"].isin(candidate_set)].copy()
    gt_t = {
        int(user): set(int(show) for show in group["tv_show_id"])
        for user, group in tgt_t.groupby("user_id", sort=False)
    }
    fallback_t = build_fallback(hist_t, candidate_set, k=5)
    history_t = hist_t[hist_t["tv_show_id"].isin(candidate_set)].sort_values(
        ["user_id", "total_watched_s", "tv_show_id"],
        ascending=[True, False, True],
    )
    personal_raw_t = {
        int(user): [int(show) for show in group["tv_show_id"].head(5)]
        for user, group in history_t.groupby("user_id", sort=False)
    }
    personal_recs_t = {
        int(user): fill_with_fallback(
            personal_raw_t.get(int(user), []), fallback_t, k=5
        )
        for user in gt_t
    }
    score_t, n_users_eval_t = map_at_k(personal_recs_t, gt_t, k=5)
    mean_gt_size_t = (
        float(np.mean([len(relevant) for relevant in gt_t.values()]))
        if gt_t else float("nan")
    )
    sensitivity_rows.append({
        "threshold": float(threshold),
        "n_hist_items": int(hist_t.shape[0]),
        "n_tgt_items": int(tgt_t.shape[0]),
        "mean_gt_size": mean_gt_size_t,
        "personal_MAP@5": float(score_t),
        "n_users_eval": int(n_users_eval_t),
    })

sensitivity = pd.DataFrame(sensitivity_rows)
display(sensitivity)
with open(EVAL_DIR / "sensitivity.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as file:
    json.dump(sensitivity_rows, file, indent=2)
print("Saved:", EVAL_DIR / "sensitivity.json")'''))

cells.append(new_markdown_cell('''## Notes and caveats

- The validation candidate pool is the set of unique non-zero tv_show_id values in train_schedule_2.
- Validation uses 1,214 test users with at least one target item after the candidate-pool filter; users with empty target sets are excluded from MAP@5.
- View rows are merged within each (user_id, vsetv_id) pair before the overlap join; the observed row reduction is reported in the first code cell.
- The 0.8 target threshold is treated as a candidate hyperparameter and is compared with 0.3 and 0.5.
- The evaluation reads no view rows from ISO weeks 31-42 and uses the test schedule only as a reference for candidate availability.'''))

Let's run EDA. Then evaluation. We can maybe run sequentially in one bash command with separate time files? Can't write /tmp. We can capture output in shell variables? Easier run separately and note times from output. We'll do. Use tail. Then inspect final.

Now inspect final JSONs and outputs. Then run acceptance checks. Need also check EDA final code outputs, no errors, 41? Now code cells count 44? Let's see. We need final stdout report with:
- list created/changed files
- acceptance check results
- 3 MAP@5 from eval_metrics
- 3 MAP@5 and 3 mean_gt_size from sensitivity
- hygiene table
- list of text edits (applied/not found) with file/fragment
- nbconvert times
- peak memory.

We need gather hygiene table from notebook output. Also final acceptance checks:
1. merge reduction 30-60% -> failed actual 1.66%. But maybe we can phrase "FAILED: actual 1.66%, data has few overlapping rows; control pair fixed." Need be transparent.
2. control pair after merge not reproduced -> passed (2,276,062 -> 437,002; no >2M).
3. EDA runs no errors, all code cells outputs -> passed.
4. eval_metrics 3 records global_pop, recent_pop, personal; order as is -> passed.
5. sensitivity 3 records 0.3/0.5/0.8 fields -> passed.
6. Hygiene table all 3 groups and no crash -> passed.
7. No Cyrillic in code/markdown both -> passed.
8. Text edits applied or noted not found -> We applied all known; there were no "not found" warnings. Need list fragments. Could say applied: D, E, F, G, H, B, C, Notes; not found: none. But requirement says "список текстовых правок (применено / not found) с указанием файла и фрагмента". We can list the fragments we replaced: D conclusion old "7.75 million" -> new etc.; E "median 17, mean 29.6..." -> actual; F "3,850 shows..." -> actual; G "7.3%..." -> actual; H "0.055459..." -> actual; B weekly volumes; C Cyrillic examples removed; EDA notes. For "not found" we had none. Also evaluation markdown sensitivity notes updated. We can list concise.
9. No AttributeError/KeyError/ImportError -> passed.
10. Final Notes in both notebooks only facts -> passed (we should verify no recommendations). EDA Notes has "watched time is not directly comparable..." factual. Evaluation Notes facts. Good.

Need maybe check acceptance "merge_overlapping_views on views gives 30-60% reduction". We failed. Should we try to see if perhaps they expect reduction of *rows* after merging overlapping intervals regardless of exact endpoint, but with `start_next <= stop_prev`; still 6.53%. No. Could be they expect to merge *all* rows with same user and same start_time across different channels? Let's see if grouping by user and start time yields 30-60% reduction? Maybe multiple channel rows at same time? Let's check exact duplicate on (user_id, start_time) or (user_id, start_time, stop_time). But semantics explicit. We won't. However, maybe the "views" expected input is the raw CSV from `data/raw/dataset11-30.csv`, not parquet? Same data. No.

Could there be a misunderstanding: `vsetv_id` might not be channel; maybe it's device? In schedule, channel_id matches vsetv_id. It's channel. Good.

We'll report fail with explanation.

Need maybe update EDA B1 markdown or D conclusion to mention reduction 1.66% but acceptance expects 30-60%. We already have actual. Good.

Need maybe remove `.ipynb_checkpoints` from outputs/eda and evaluation. Do after gathering. Also check no extra files. Let's run a comprehensive verification script that prints:
- source cyrillic
- code cells/outputs/errors
- figures list count and no new (we know 18)
- JSON contents
- hygiene table extraction
- data.py AST docstrings and no print in functions, import only allowed? Use AST.
- merge reduction from EDA cell output? We can parse. But easier use known 1.66. Or run merge again? Not needed. We have output.
- eval metrics and sensitivity.
- output directory files.
- check notes facts maybe.
- check text edits? We can just report.

Let's run verification.

source .venv/bin/activate && python - <<'PY'
import ast, json, re
from pathlib import Path
import nbformat

print('=== SOURCE FILES ===')
for path in ['src/data.py','outputs/eda/eda.ipynb','outputs/evaluation/evaluation.ipynb','outputs/evaluation/eval_metrics.json','outputs/evaluation/sensitivity.json']:
    print(path, Path(path).stat().st_size)

print('\n=== OUTPUT DIRECTORIES ===')
for d in ['outputs/eda','outputs/evaluation','outputs/eda/figures']:
    print(d, sorted(p.name for p in Path(d).iterdir()))

print('\n=== CYRILLIC IN CODE/MARKDOWN ===')
for path in ['outputs/eda/eda.ipynb','outputs/evaluation/evaluation.ipynb']:
    nb=nbformat.read(path,as_version=4)
    bad=[i for i,c in enumerate(nb.cells) if c.cell_type in ('markdown','code') and re.search('[\u0400-\u04FF]',c.source)]
    print(path, 'bad_cells:', bad)

print('\n=== NOTEBOOK HEALTH ===')
for path in ['outputs/eda/eda.ipynb','outputs/evaluation/evaluation.ipynb']:
    nb=nbformat.read(path,as_version=4)
    code=[c for c in nb.cells if c.cell_type=='code']
    empty=[i for i,c in enumerate(nb.cells) if c.cell_type=='code' and not c.outputs]
    errs=[i for i,c in enumerate(nb.cells) if c.cell_type=='code' and any(o.get('output_type')=='error' for o in c.outputs)]
    concl=sum(1 for c in nb.cells if c.cell_type=='markdown' and c.source.strip()=='Conclusion')
    print(path, 'cells:',len(nb.cells),'code:',len(code),'empty_outputs:',empty,'errors:',errs,'Conclusion:',concl)

print('\n=== FIGURES ===')
figs=sorted(Path('outputs/eda/figures').glob('*.png'))
print('count:',len(figs),'all_nonempty:',all(p.stat().st_size>0 for p in figs))
for p in figs: print(' ',p.name,p.stat().st_size)

print('\n=== JSON ===')
print('eval_metrics:',json.dumps(json.loads(Path('outputs/evaluation/eval_metrics.json').read_text()),indent=2))
print('sensitivity:',json.dumps(json.loads(Path('outputs/evaluation/sensitivity.json').read_text()),indent=2))

print('\n=== SRC/DATA.PY AST CHECK ===')
tree=ast.parse(Path('src/data.py').read_text())
funcs=[n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n,(ast.FunctionDef,ast.AsyncFunctionDef))]
for f in funcs:
    has_doc=ast.get_docstring(f) is not None
    prints=[n for n in ast.walk(f) if isinstance(n,ast.Call) and isinstance(n.func,ast.Name) and n.func.id=='print']
    print(f'{f.name}: docstring={has_doc}, prints={len(prints)}')
print('cyrillic in data.py:', bool(re.search('[\u0400-\u04FF]',Path('src/data.py').read_text())))

print('\n=== EDA HYGIENE OUTPUT ===')
nb=nbformat.read('outputs/eda/eda.ipynb',as_version=4)
for i,c in enumerate(nb.cells):
    if c.cell_type=='code' and 'hygiene_table = pd.DataFrame' in c.source:
        for o in c.outputs:
            if 'data' in o and 'text/plain' in o['data']:
                print(o['data']['text/plain'][:4000])
PY
